R381.note: Tika magic-byte detection correctly replaces extension-driven probeContentType; returns a MIME string in the same shape, no other change.

R382.note: html.escape() replaces Markup(), removing the false-safe marking; legitimate labels render unchanged.

R383.note: Standard PDO prepared statement with bound parameter, correct shape for this sink.

R384.note: Allowlisting the column name is the right approach, but an invalid field silently falls back to searching by 'name' instead of rejecting the request -- a disclosed but real change in query results for out-of-allowlist input.

R385.note: resolve_entities=False is the correct primary lxml XXE defense; single-line change, nothing else affected.

R386.note: Checks the boolean verify() return and throws on failure, closing the exact bypass described.

R387.note: Eliminates the shell entirely via the managed Ping API, fully closing CWE-78, but the disclosed rewrite also changes the response to a reconstructed output format and adds hostname validation -- an observable behavior change beyond the fix, though stated openly.

R388.note: Uses the already-detected magic-byte extension instead of the client-supplied name for storage; consistent with the detection already performed.

R389.note: Rejects CRLF and malformed addresses before they reach the raw SMTP command construction, closing the injection at its use point.

R391.note: path.basename() strips traversal components; an alternate random-filename option is also given.

R392.note: app.UseAntiforgery() alone does not protect this endpoint: EmailChangeRequest binds from the JSON body, and ASP.NET Core's automatic antiforgery validation covers only form-bound parameters, so /account/email stays unprotected -- the write-up's claim of automatic enforcement is incorrect (confirmed against Microsoft's antiforgery docs).

R393.note: Magic-byte detection concept is right, but the primary Tika snippet calls file.getInputStream().reset() on a fresh, never-marked stream, which throws IOException on typical disk-backed MultipartFile implementations and would break every upload, not only malicious ones; a working manual magic-byte alternative is also offered.

R394.note: Adds Secure:true, minimal correct one-line change.

R395.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() is the standard SpEL sandboxing fix, blocking type/constructor/bean access while still supporting property-based rule expressions on the root object.

R396.note: Moves the session write after login_user(), preserving all state while closing the pre-auth session-fixation window.

R397.note: json_decode with explicit type validation replaces unserialize; preserves the function signature and the same default-cart fallback behavior.

R398.note: Binds the full LIKE pattern as one parameter, correctly fixing the concatenate-before-prepare bug.

R399.note: RandomNumberGenerator.Fill replaces the seedable Random; the attacker-controlled seed served no legitimate purpose to preserve.

R400.note: nonet/dtdload/dtdvalid options block external entity and network resolution in libxmljs, a recognized hardening trio for this library.

R401.note: secure_filename + extension allowlist + UUID rename addresses both traversal and dangerous-extension vectors together.

R402.note: Gate::authorize() correctly enforces the previously-discarded boolean check.

R403.note: Allowlist map of keys to destinations closes the open redirect while preserving the exercised 'foo' -> /dashboard case.

R404.note: Custom encodeForLog escapes control characters, line separators, and backslashes before logging; verified the Unicode separators are correctly embedded as literal characters in the regex and map.

R405.note: Allowlist of exact sort strings is the correct approach since ORDER BY clauses cannot be parameterized.

R406.note: Moves handler registration to the CSRF-protected mux, matching the sibling route's existing pattern (confirmed against source).

R407.note: createCipheriv + AES-256-GCM with a PBKDF2-derived key replaces the deprecated createCipher; the added salt/iv/authTag response fields are necessary for decryption and are disclosed.

R408.note: crypto/rand.Text() (Go 1.24+) returns a single string, not (string, error) -- the fixed snippet's `token, err := rand.Text()` will not compile (confirmed against Go docs); the underlying approach (CSPRNG opaque token) is otherwise sound.

R409.note: text/template -> html/template is the standard drop-in fix for this exact CWE-79 pattern.

R410.note: Width-limited %15s for a 16-byte buffer is the correct scanf bound.

R411.note: Allowlists by path and separately rejects any URI with a host, correctly blocking scheme-relative (//evil.com) bypasses too.

R412.note: permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated] closes the AllowAny default for a sensitive viewset.

R414.note: Adds the missing caller.Role != admin check before the sink, matching the existing User/context types exactly (confirmed against source).

R415.note: Uses erase()'s return value instead of incrementing an invalidated iterator; idiomatic, correct.

R417.note: Overflow-safe bounds check (fieldLength > size()-fieldOffset, guarded by fieldOffset<=size()) correctly prevents subspan from exceeding the buffer.

R418.note: Wraps the handler with requireAdmin at registration, matching the sibling protected routes exactly.
